newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng at record close driven by liquidity.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng at record close driven by liquidity.

text.p: Kong Hong stocks extended their record-breaking rally on Friday and the Hang Seng Index eked out a closing high, but trade was volatile with profit-taking on banks and utilities alternating with buying on property stocks.
The Hang Seng ended at 16,379.22, up 13.51 points, or 0.08 percent, after touching an intra-day high of 16,449.53 earlier.
Turnover was the second highest ever at HK$26.98 billion, though down slightly from Thursday's record HK$28.03 billion.
"Liquidity flowing in from Southeast Asia and other places helped lift the Hang Seng further," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
Buying was focused on properties while banks and utilities met some profit-taking after recent sharp gains, Kwong said.
Sun Hung Kai Properties surged HK$3.75 to HK$101.00 and Cheung Kong was up HK$1.25 to HK$87.25.
"This rally is led by properties, and the laggards in the sector and property developers should continue to see buyers," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J&A Securities.

Brokers said properties had largely lagged behind recent market gains and investors were also buying on hopes that local property prices would bottom out soon after the government said there was no current need to take measures against speculators.
Bank of East Asia fell HK$0.10 to close at HK$32.10 after the bank announced a 21.7 percent rise on its interim net profit.
"The results are in line with market expectations but some feared that it may not be able to keep up such good growth in the second half, so they took profits," Cheung said.
Other blue-chip banks were lower. HSBC Holdings fell HK$2.00 to HK$268.00 and Hang Seng Bank lost HK$0.50 to HK$112.50.
Hopewell rose HK$0.125 to HK$4.85 on speculation that Chinese interests might take a stake in the company.
Cheung said the market was likely to head for a brief consolidation early next week but the underlying tone remained positive.
The red-chip index added 38.97 points, or 1.09 percent, to 3,613.64 and the H-share index edged up 10.57 points, or 0.84 percent, to 1,268.16.
Beijing Enterprises surged HK$2.70 to HK$52.00 on hopes that its mainland parent would inject good quality projects to the company later this year.
COSCO Pacific jumped HK$0.55 to HK$17.90.
